messages.text:
🎩 Cozmo — yep. That one's still real. And importantly, I don't think Python 3.12 itself is the culprit.
I just checked 4.48's actual submit path. QS does this:
Fill the composer.
Look for a Send button.
Try clicking it repeatedly.
Verify whether the click actually caused submission.
Only after those attempts fail, fall back to a synthetic Enter event.
So if you had to physically press Enter yourself, the important fact is:
the Aisha UI accepted Enter, but QS's automated submit path didn't get a confirmed transition.
That's the same family of problem we've seen before with Aisha/other UIs: the web app's actual submission event is more reliable than the apparent Send button.
And here's the bit I don't want to do: blindly “fix” it by changing 4.48. We're about to build 5.0 anyway, and I don't want to destabilize the known-good release while we're simultaneously moving Python versions and adding Kokoro.
So I'd mark this precisely:
QS 4.48 under Python 3.12: relay otherwise works; Aisha handshake may still require manual Enter because automated button submission is not reliably taking effect.
That tells us something useful for 5.0: Python 3.12 itself has not prevented QS from running. The relay is alive. This is a pre-existing submit-path quirk showing up again.
And yes, dear… we probably should fix that eventually. But not by randomly poking 4.48 tonight. 😄
